original_question: I read about some researchers who were trying to produce sperm from bone marrow stem cells. If a woman were to have sperm cells made from her own stem cells and impregnate herself, what would be her relationship to her daughter?
short_answer_summary: The hypothetical child inherits only the parent's variants, but loses much of their paired diversity; the source estimates an inbreeding coefficient of 0.5.
detailed_scientific_explanation: The source reviews preliminary stem-cell-to-sperm research, distinguishing spermatogonial or sperm-like cells from functional sperm and noting a 2009 paper's retraction for plagiarism. It then uses a deliberately simplified D&D model: seven chromosomes, six stats plus sex; each parent has two variants; gametes randomly select one version. Numbers and multipliers illustrate favorable heterozygous combinations and harmful identical pairs. Self-fertilization independently samples twice from the same parent, so about half the child's loci receive identical variants from one parental copy. No Y donor means a female child in the simplified setup. Recessive harmful variants become more likely to pair, exemplified by spinal muscular atrophy; sickle-cell variation illustrates a heterozygote advantage with homozygote harm. The parent possesses all the child's variants but the child lacks some of the parent's. The resulting inbreeding coefficient is 0.50, likened to several generations of sibling mating, and severe health risks are expected. The analogy is not a literal chromosome-to-stat map; real genetics and reproductive biology are more complex.
initial_assumptions: Hypothetical functional gametes from one woman
Seven-stat toy model replaces real 23 chromosome pairs

quantitative_facts.value: Toy combination rule: two numbers → greater; number×multiplier; two multipliers →1
Toy Alice/Bob child stats STR15 CON10 DEX14 CHR15 WIS16 INT28, female
Toy self-fertilized child STR15 CON1 DEX14 CHR16 WIS7 INT14, female
Toy double-multiplier probability 58% versus 25%; expected identical copies at 50% of loci; SMA figures 1/50 carrier, 1/100 transmitted, 1/10,000 two-parent risk and 1/400 selfed risk as printed
quantitative_facts.uncertainty: SMA arithmetic as printed mixes carrier/transmission probabilities; verify independently before reuse.

quantitative_facts.value: Inbreeding coefficient 0.50; cited estimate 22-point IQ reduction and 4-inch height reduction at age ten; Charles II coefficient 0.254; sibling child 0.250

footnotes.note: Some SMA forms involve two genes, complicating statistics.
Some all-female salamanders use male sperm to stimulate egg laying without self-fertilization; text distinguishes asexual reproduction.

uncertainties_and_limitations: Toy D&D model explicitly simplified and table entries vary between examples
Population estimates and historical clinical predictions need verification; not individual prognosis
extraction_notes: Source transcript is machine OCR and requires line-by-line proofreading against page images.
